content: 1. The results from the de novo review and meta-analysis indicate that the evidence was downgraded by two levels for risk of bias because more than 30% of the included studies demonstrated a high risk of bias in certain domains. 2. The evidence was downgraded by two levels for inconsistency due to considerable and highly significant heterogeneity observed across the studies. 3. The evidence was downgraded by one level for imprecision because the 95% confidence interval (CI) spanned both important benefit and unimportant harm. 4. The evidence was downgraded by one level for publication bias, as suggested by an asymmetrical funnel plot. 5. The evidence was downgraded by two levels for imprecision when the 95% CI spanned both important benefit and important harm. 6. The evidence was downgraded by one level for indirectness because only one study was available to inform the outcome. 7. The evidence was downgraded by one level for inconsistency due to moderate heterogeneity observed in the results. 8. The guidelines on mental health promotive and preventive interventions for adolescents exposed to humanitarian emergencies highlight the need for further research to determine the effectiveness of psychosocial interventions in preventing aggressive, disruptive, and oppositional behaviors compared to treatment as usual. 9. The certainty of evidence for psychosocial interventions promoting positive mental health for pregnant or parenting adolescents was rated as very low, indicating a lack of confidence in the effect estimate. 10. Psychosocial interventions likely make little or no difference to mental disorders in pregnant or parenting adolescents when compared to treatment as usual, with the certainty of evidence rated as low. 11. It is unclear whether psychosocial interventions prevent substance use in pregnant or parenting adolescents when compared to treatment as usual, with the certainty of evidence rated as very low. 12. The effectiveness of psychosocial interventions in preventing risky sexual behaviors in pregnant or parenting adolescents remains unknown, with the certainty of evidence rated as very low. 13. Psychosocial interventions were found to promote school attendance for pregnant or parenting adolescents when compared to treatment as usual, with the certainty of evidence rated as high. 14. Psychosocial interventions may slightly promote adherence to antenatal and postnatal care for pregnant or parenting adolescents when compared to treatment as usual, with the certainty of evidence rated as low. 15. It is not known whether psychosocial interventions improve parenting skills for pregnant or parenting adolescents when compared to treatment as usual, with the certainty of evidence rated as very low. 16. Exposure to intimate partner violence was not reported in the included studies, highlighting a gap in the evidence base. 17. The risk in the intervention group, along with its 95% confidence interval, is based on the assumed risk in the comparison group and the relative effect of the intervention. 18. Approximate odds ratios (ORs) were calculated using logarithmic transformation of standardized mean differences (SMDs) according to the method by Hasselblad and Hedges (1995). Where the SMD was lower in the intervention group, the reciprocal value of the approximation was determined. 19. The GRADE Working Group grades of evidence indicate that high certainty means the true effect is very likely to be close to the estimate, while very low certainty means the true effect is likely to be substantially different from the estimate.
